claim: PLYFLD is $1000, 30 wide by 32 high; a DDTADD high byte therefore carries the $10 page plus the column-page in its low 2 bits (offset = ((hi&3)<<8)|lo, row = lo&$1F, col-page = lo>>5 within hi&3).
NDDT = 4: the DDTADD bank holds exactly four bomb entries per player.
CLOUD = $2E is the first DDT-explosion-cloud stamp; the cloud band is [$2E, $6E).
DDT = $6E is the first of the 2 stamps for a DDT bomb: DDT at the base cell, DDT+1 = $6F at base+$20 (next column, same row).

source.verbatim: DDT	=6E			;FIRST OF 2 STAMPS FOR DDT BOMB

claim: ROCK = $70. In DDTS2 the masked stamp is compared against ROCK: cells holding $01..$6F block the restore write, cells >= $70 (rocks and all mushroom pictures) are overwritten.
DELAY is the between-waves delay byte; BOMBS sets it to $80 and bomb-mode arming sets it to $40.

source.verbatim: DELAY:	.BLKB 1			;NON ZERO TO DELY BETWEEN WAVES

claim: HITDDT is non-zero once a DDT has been hit; shooting a bomb increments it.

source.verbatim: HITDDT:	.BLKB 2			;NON-ZERO IF DDT HAS BEEN HIT

claim: NOCENT is the bomb-mode critter budget: non-zero means critters (not centipedes) are to be started.

source.verbatim: NOCENT:	.BLKB 1			;NON-ZERO IF NO CENTIPEDES ARE TO BE STARTED

claim: DDTADD is the player-1 bank of NDDT*2 address bytes (lo at DDTADD-1+X, hi at DDTADD+X, X = 7,5,3,1); D5-D7 of the high byte carry the explosion sequence.

source.verbatim: DDTADD:	.BLKB NDDT*2		;PLAYER 1 DDT BOMB ADDRESSES (D5-D7=EXPLOSION SEQUENCE)

claim: The player-2 DDTADD bank follows player 1; DDTS1 selects it with PLAYR<<3 (caller/wiring concern - the core models one bank).
DDTS is the "ADD DDT BOMBS" routine: wave-start placement of the DDTADD bank followed by the DDTS2 stamp restore.
DDTS copies NDDT*2 = 8 address bytes (4 word entries) from DDTST into DDTADD, Y descending from NDDT*2-1.
DDTS tests MODE EOR $FF: only MODE == $FF (special attract) switches to the special DDT placements.
Special attract mode uses DDTST bytes $17..$10, i.e. words 8..11 of DDTST ($10A3, $1084, $1086, 0).
Upright non-attract placement copies DDTST bytes $07..$00, i.e. words 0..3 ($10CD, $1119, $1233, $12F7).
The DDTST bytes are stored into DDTADD with X descending in lockstep with Y: entry pair (X=7,6) receives word 3, (5,4) word 2, (3,2) word 1, (1,0) word 0.
DDTS2 re-stamps every intact table entry onto the playfield; it is also called standalone to restore bombs blanked by messages.
A zero DDTADD high byte means a vacant entry: DDTS2 skips it.
The exploding threshold is the high byte >= PLYFLD+400/100 = $14.
DDTS2 does not re-stamp an exploding entry.
DDTS2 writes the second stamp cell at entry address + $20 (upright picture order: DDT+1 first at +$20).
A cell whose masked stamp (AND $7F) is zero is writable.
The occupancy test compares the masked stamp against ROCK ($70).

source.verbatim: CMP I,ROCK		;WE CAN OVERWRITE A MUSHROOM IN ATTRACT

claim: Masked stamps $01..$6F block the write (letters, clouds, other bombs); >= ROCK falls through and is overwritten ("WE CAN OVERWRITE A MUSHROOM IN ATTRACT").
The +$20 cell receives stamp DDT+1 = $6F.
The window flips back (Y EOR $20) to the base cell.
The base cell receives stamp DDT = $6E.
DDTS1 computes the bank index X = (PLAYR<<3) | (NDDT*2-1): player 1 sweeps X = 7,5,3,1 - table entries are visited word-3-first (descending).
DDTS1 sets the sweep counter TEMP2 = NDDT-1 = 3: exactly four entries are visited.
DDTST word 0 is $10CD (upright word 0); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 1 is $1119 (upright word 1); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 2 is $1233 (upright word 2); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 3 is $12F7 (upright word 3); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 4 is $12F2 (cocktail player-2 word 4); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 5 is $12A6 (cocktail word 5); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 6 is $118C (cocktail word 6); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 7 is $10C8 (cocktail word 7); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 8 is $10A3 (special-attract word 8); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 9 is $1084 (special-attract word 9); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 10 is $1086 (special-attract word 10); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
DDTST word 11 is 0 (special-attract word 11 - a vacant fourth entry); the table is exactly 12 words - upright 0..3, cocktail 4..7, special attract 8..11.
Game start calls DDTS2 to reset the DDT bomb stamps (wiring seam for ml7).
After a message overlay the game jumps to DDTS2 to restore the bombs (wiring seam).
A second message path also restores blanked bombs via DDTS2 (wiring seam).

source.verbatim: JMP DDTS2		;RESTORE ANY DDT BOMBS BLANKED OUT

claim: The scroll gate ORs the four DDTADD high bytes and compares the OR against $14: sound only because intact pages are $10..$12 - the seed rejection of column-page 3 keeps the OR below the threshold.
MUSHD1 derives the count region from the address low byte AND $1F (the row).
Upright: rows < $0C decrement MUSH (the bottom-region count).

source.verbatim: BCC 7$			;IF MUSHROOM IS ON LOWER HALF OF SCREEN

claim: Upright: rows $0C..$13 decrement NOTHING - the middle band is uncounted.
Rows >= $14 fall through INX INX and decrement MUSH+2 (the top-region count).
Down-scroll clears the one-bomb-per-line flag first: at most ONE bomb is seeded per scroll.

source.verbatim: STA TEMP2+1		;ALLOW ONLY 1 DDT BOMB PER LINE

claim: A vacant entry (hi = 0) goes to the seeding branch.
An exploding entry (hi >= $14) is neither moved nor cleared by the scroll.
Upright down-scroll moves the bomb pointer with DEC lo (one row down).
The off-screen test masks the moved lo with $1E (row bits sans bit 0): rows 0 and 1 both read as off-screen.
lo AND $1E == 0 clears the entry (hi = 0); the stamps are NOT erased by this path - the field shift already moved them.
A second vacant entry in the same scroll finds the flag set and does not seed.
Seed column page = RND1 AND 3; the value 3 is rejected ("STAY AWAY FROM THE RIGHT EDGE") - bombs never occupy column page 3.
The accepted page is ORed with PLYFLD/100 = $10 to form the entry high byte.
Seed lo takes its column-low bits from RND0 AND $E0.
Seed lo ORs in $1E: new bombs enter on the top row.
Left-edge guard: lo >= $80 is always acceptable.
lo < $80 with page $10 (columns 0..3) rejects the seed; lo < $80 on pages $11/$12 is fine.

source.verbatim: BEQ 68$			;NO DDT BOMBS (STAY AWAY FROM LEFT EDGE)

claim: The one-per-scroll flag is set with the current table index X (7,5,3,1 - always non-zero).

source.verbatim: 64$:	STX TEMP2+1		;NON-ZERO=FLAG FOR NO MORE DDT BOMBS

claim: A non-zero byte at seed+$20 decrements MUSH+2 before being overwritten (the seed row is in the top region).
The seed writes DDT+1 at address+$20 ...
... decrements MUSH+2 again if the base cell is non-zero ...
... and writes DDT at the base address.
Up-scroll skips vacant entries; there is NO seeding on up-scroll.
Up-scroll skips exploding entries.
Upright up-scroll moves the bomb pointer with INC lo (one row up).
The off-top test is (lo AND $1F) EOR $1F: only row $1F reads as off the top.
A bomb reaching row $1F is cleared (hi = 0).
The up-scroll DDT half tails into SCROL0 (obstacle-on-player unstick - ml3-3 seam).

source.verbatim: JMP SCROL0		;REMOVE OBSTACLE ON TOP OF PLAYER.

claim: BOMBS is the bomb-mode critter-entry dispatcher: it bombs the player with bee, mosquito and dragonfly.

source.verbatim: .SBTTL	BOMBS - BOMB PLAYER WITH BEE, MOSQUITO AND DRAGONFLY

claim: NOCENT == 0 returns immediately (no delay set).
Special attract mode (MODE bit 7 set) never bombs (no delay set).
The entry gate is RND0 AND 7 == 0 (a fresh RND0 read).
Once the gates pass, DELAY = $80 is set BEFORE the slot scan - it is set even when no free slot is found.

source.verbatim: STA DELAY		;WAIT UNTIL THEY REACH THE BOTTOM

claim: The slot scan starts at index 12 decimal (13 BEEC slots, 12..0).
A zero BEEC byte is a free slot; finding one proceeds to the creature dispatch.
No free slot in 12..0 returns (with DELAY already set).
The creature-table index is CENTIN >> 1 (0..5 for CENTIN 0..11).
A creature code with D7 = 1 takes the dragonfly/mosquito path; D7 = 0 (codes $00) enters a bee directly.
The bee entry calls BEEMV3 (the ml4-3 bee spawn seam).
Every successful entry decrements NOCENT by exactly one.

source.verbatim: DEC NOCENT		;JUST SO SPEED IS AT LEAST 2

claim: After ASL: negative (code $C0 -> $80) means mosquitoes only.
After ASL: zero (code $80 -> $00) means dragonflies only.
The multi-critter mask ANDs a SECOND, separate RND0 read - the gate read (bits 0-2 clear) must not be reused or the dispatch degenerates to always-bee.
Masked pick == 0 enters a bee.
Masked pick == 6 enters a mosquito (only reachable for code $83, mask 6).
Any other masked pick enters a dragonfly via FLYMV3 (the ml4-2 seam).
The mosquito entry calls MOSQT3 (the ml4-2 seam).
The creature table is $83,$81,$C0,$80 for CENTIN pairs 0-1,2-3,4-5,6-7 ...
... and $80,$00 for pairs 8-9,10-11: late-wave pairs are dragonflies-only then bees-only.
BOMBSL lists the CENTIN values that arm bomb mode: 1,3,5,7 ...
... and $0B - five arming levels in all.
At wave end, CENTIN is matched against the five BOMBSL entries (Y = 4..0); a match arms bomb mode.

source.verbatim: 55$:	CMP Y,BOMBSL		;IS THIS THE LEVEL TO BOMB THE PLAYER

claim: NOCENT = (SCORE2 >> 1) + 20 decimal + the LSR carry: there is NO CLC, so an odd SCORE2 adds one extra critter (the BEEMV1-style carry trap).
The computed budget is stored in NOCENT.
Arming increments BOMBV (bomb-mode scoring flag - wiring seam).

source.verbatim: INC BOMBV		;START GIVING SCORES FOR BOMB MODE

claim: Arming sets DELAY = $40 so the centipede does not start during the bombing.

source.verbatim: STA DELAY		;DELAY ATTRACT MODE SO CENTIPEDE DOES NOT START.

claim: Explosions advance only on frames where FRAME AND 7 == 0 (every 8th frame).
The cloud anchor low byte is the entry lo - it does not change during the explosion.
Only entries with high byte >= $14 are advanced.
The next state is high byte - $10 (SBC with carry known set).
The anchor high byte is (new hi AND 3) OR $10 - the position survives in the low 2 bits.
The frame index derives from the OLD high byte: AND $F0 then four LSRs.
The four LSRs leave carry CLEAR, so SBC #1 subtracts 2: index = (old hi >> 4) - 2, giving 9..0 from start value $B4.
Index 0 clears the entry (hi = 0) and still runs list 0 - the final erase frame.

source.verbatim: STA X,DDTADD		;CLEAR DDT ENTRY IF DONE

claim: The 98$ table maps index 0..9 to an offset-list start; offsets and stamps are PARALLEL tables read with the same cursor.
Each offset list is terminated by $FF.
A blank cell (masked stamp 0) is overwritten.
Masked stamps < CLOUD (letters/digits) are PRESERVED.
Masked stamps in [CLOUD, DDT) - existing cloud pictures - are overwritten.
Masked stamps DDT and DDT+1 - other bombs - are PRESERVED.

source.verbatim: BCC 84$			;DO NOT DESTROY LETTERS OR DDT BOMBS

claim: Masked stamps >= DDT+2 = $70 (rocks included) are destroyed AND counted via MUSHD1 region rules.
Every write preserves bit 7 (the grey player-area background) and ORs in the parallel 99$ stamp.

SHOOT1: masked stamps < CLOUD are the letter path (not DDT).
SHOOT1: a stamp in the cloud band returns ZERO status - the shot flies straight through an explosion cloud.
SHOOT1: stamp == DDT ($6E, the base cell) is a bomb hit.
SHOOT1: stamp == DDT+1 ($6F, the +$20 cell) is also a bomb hit.
Upright: a DDT+1 hit normalizes the address by -$20 to the entry base before the table match.

source.verbatim: SBC I,20		;PUT PICTURE WINDOW IN CORRECT POSITION

claim: The hit address is matched against the DDTADD bank byte-for-byte (hi then lo).
No table match returns zero status (the bomb "must be starting to explode").

source.verbatim: BPL 30$			;DDT MUST BE STARTING TO EXPLODE

claim: The hit clears the base stamp keeping only bit 7 (grey) ...

source.verbatim: AND I,80		;SAVE COLOR FOR PLAYERS AREA

claim: ... and stores the SAME byte at +$20 - the +$20 cell inherits the BASE cell's grey bit, not its own.
The entry lo becomes base - $61: the cloud anchor is 3 columns left and 1 row up of the bomb.
The entry hi becomes (borrow-adjusted page) OR $B4: exploding, first frame index 9.
Hitting a DDT bomb scores 80 points.

source.verbatim: JSR SCORNG		;80 POINTS FOR HITTING DDT

claim: Hitting a DDT bomb increments HITDDT.
The hit starts sound CHAN2 = $24 (wiring seam - core stays silent).
DDTEXP: a stamp >= CLOUD ...
... and < DDT is inside a cloud; anything else exits with carry clear (no kill).
DDTEX1 passes A = $80 (negative = killed-by-DDT) into SHOOT2 - the flag that triples critter scores.
The kill itself is SHOOT2 dispatch (the per-critter reducers own their scores - ml4-1/2/3 seams).

MOTION's DDT-cloud kill reads the cell the segment NOW OCCUPIES: after the move (:1601-1608), OBSTAC is called with Y=0 (LDY I,0), so the 8*DIR term vanishes and it looks at (H,V) itself, NOT the cell-ahead the turn check (:1527 OBSTA0, Y=DIR) reads.

Per-segment DDT-cloud collision: MOTION calls DDTEXP on the occupied cell's stamp every step - this is the segment-kill wiring (a millipede segment marching onto a DDT cloud dies), distinct from the shot-vs-bomb detonation (SHOOT1).

source.verbatim: JSR DDTEXP		;CHECK FOR DDT CLOUD COLLISION

claim: DDTEXP carry-set means the segment was DESTROYED: MOTION branches to 30$ (next entry), skipping BOTH the player-collision PLAY (:1615) and the direction-change turn (:1621-1631) - a killed segment neither hurts the player nor turns.

SHOOT2's millipede branch (142$) leaves a mushroom at the dead segment's cell (MUSHER) and DECs DEAD - so a DDT-cloud kill both removes the segment from the live count and plants a mushroom, exactly as a shot kill does.

A DDT-cloud kill scores 30 for a BODY segment: SHOOT2 142$ loads the base LDA I,10 (BODY=10) then, because DDTEX1 always set the DDT-death flag (DD-217), overrides it to LDA I,30 (BIT TEMP3+1 / BPL 16$ falls through) — so a DDT body kill is BCD 30, tripled from the base 10.

A HEAD scores in the hundreds: SHOOT2 142$ LSR×4's the score byte into the high digit (100 POINTS FOR A HEAD), so the DDT-death value 30 becomes 300 (0x30 >> 4 = 3 → 3*100), tripled from a shot head's 100.
